statements.status_notes: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty. Netty attempts to read OS identification files even on Windows systems where they don't natively exist. An attacker with local access can create an oversized (>1GB) file at these paths, causing Netty to load it into memory and exhaust the JVM heap, crashing the application.
statements.impact_statement: Netty's PlatformDependent unconditionally attempts to read /etc/os-release and /usr/lib/os-release-style paths for OS identification, including on Windows where these paths don't natively exist. Exploitation requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access sufficient to plant a >1GB file at one of these root-level paths ahead of JVM startup — a precondition that itself requires the host to already be compromised at a level exceeding what this DoS provides. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

statements.status_notes: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 VerifyHostname quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib versions in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images. The Secure Dockerfile installs lpm as an optional helper (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49), but the Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); otherwise it executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119). A focused grep across the Docker runtime files found no direct VerifyHostname, Certificate.Verify, matchHostnames, HostnameError, or crypto/x509 usage. Defense in depth: current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

As established in the prior assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9, Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary.

statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. statements.status_notes: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib recursion-limit issue in Unmarshal. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-5972 alias.

statements.status_notes: Netty HttpObjectDecoder incorrectly terminates chunk header parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings in chunked transfer encoding extensions, enabling HTTP request smuggling.

Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u481-perf, 11.0.30, 17.0.18, 21.0.10, 25.0.2, 26; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.18 and 21.0.10; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.17. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE networking vulnerability. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1), not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client distribution. The container runs the Liquibase CLI through docker-entrypoint.sh rather than a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet environment (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so the client-only runtime required by the advisory is absent.

There is no attacker-controlled hostname input path here, so the Punycode hostname-validation bug is unreachable in this deployment.

statements.status_notes: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, root.Open("symlink/") will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib os.Root symlink-following vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.12, 1.26.5, and 1.27.0-rc.2. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib version v1.26.4 in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49) — confirmed by extracting the released liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 binary and running `go version` on it, which reports go1.26.4, matching the scanner's reported installed version exactly. The vulnerable API, os.Root (and OpenRoot), is a defensive filesystem-sandboxing API added in Go 1.24; a source-level grep of the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 repository for os.Root, OpenRoot, and .Root( returned zero hits, so lpm does not use the vulnerable API at all. Defense in depth: the Secure Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); the default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly and never calls lpm (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119-121).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib html/template escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no html/template usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/http/httputil ReverseProxy query sanitization vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no ReverseProxy or net/http/httputil usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: XML External Entity (XXE) via Unsanitized Dictionary Parsing in Apache OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor. Versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3 initialize dictionary XML parsing without secure processing or DTD restrictions, allowing attacker-supplied dictionary files to trigger local file disclosure or server-side request forgery during SAX parsing.
statements.impact_statement: OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor XXE vulnerability fixed in 2.5.9. Liquibase Secure declares opennlp-tools through opennlp.version 2.5.8 (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/pom.xml:76) in the phileas AI services dependency (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:18, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:19, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:20), but the vulnerable dictionary XML parsing API is not imported or called. statements.status_notes: A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent is set to true and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot ApplicationTemp exploitation requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and persistence across application restarts. Liquibase Secure's Docker image starts the Liquibase CLI entrypoint (docker/Dockerfile:68), and grep for server.servlet.session.persistent, ApplicationTemp, persistent=true, and setPersistent across Java, XML, properties, YAML, and YML files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: In certain circumstances, Spring Boot's default web security is ineffective allowing unauthorized access to all endpoints. For an application to be vulnerable, it must be a servlet-based web application, have no Spring Security configuration of its own and rely on the default web security filter chain, depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, and not depend on spring-boot-health.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot default web security bypass requires the application to depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure and not depend on spring-boot-health. The repository's only Spring Boot declaration is spring-boot-autoconfigure, provided-scope for the Pro integration (pro/pom.xml:81); grep for spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, spring-boot-starter-actuator, and spring-boot-health across pom.xml files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: Little CMS (lcms2) through 2.18 has an integer overflow in CubeSize in cmslut.c because the overflow check is performed after the multiplication.

The scan reported Oracle OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-LTS, but Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) and contains no Little CMS/lcms2 references in the repository, so the scanner's openjdk match is a false product match.

statements.status_notes: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.

The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

statements.status_notes: Applications that evaluate user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are vulnerable to an Algorithmic Denial of Service (DoS). By providing a specially crafted expression, an attacker can trigger excessive resource consumption during evaluation, leading to application degradation or unavailability.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Expression is a transitive dependency of spring-context, declared provided/optional at core/liquibase-standard/pom.xml:85. Repo search found no org.springframework.expression imports, no SpelExpressionParser, and no StandardEvaluationContext usage. The only parseExpression() hit is the custom tokenizer in commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-couchbase/src/main/java/ liquibase/ext/couchbase/provider/ExpressionDocumentKeyProvider.java:38, which does not evaluate SpEL. The reactor also pins <spring.version>7.0.8</spring.version> in core/pom.xml:79.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader is vulnerable to arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled input passed to the extension loading mechanism, potentially allowing remote code execution.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader arbitrary class instantiation vulnerability. The ExtensionLoader API is not imported or called anywhere in Liquibase Secure. The only production OpenNLP usage is document categorization and tokenization via DoccatModel, DocumentCategorizerME, and WhitespaceTokenizer in OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java; no extension loading or dynamic class instantiation occurs.

statements.status_notes: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count. With a large enough value, the client spends an unbounded amount of CPU time inside PBKDF2 before authentication can fail. A single attempt ties up a CPU core. Repeated or concurrent attempts exhaust client CPU and can wedge connection pools. In affected versions, loginTimeout did not fully mitigate this problem. When loginTimeout expired, the caller could stop waiting, but the worker thread performing the connection attempt could continue running and burning CPU inside the SCRAM PBKDF2 computation. This issue has been patched in version 42.7.11.
statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL JDBC SCRAM-SHA-256 client-side denial of service fixed in 42.7.11. Liquibase Secure distribution declares postgresql.version as 42.7.11 (dist/pom.xml:23) and uses that property for the org.postgresql:postgresql dependency (dist/pom.xml:115, dist/pom.xml:117), so the vulnerable 42.7.9 code reported by the scanner is not present in the current distribution build.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader allocates unbounded memory when reading model files, allowing a malicious or malformed model file to cause an out-of-memory denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader OOM denial-of-service vulnerability via unbounded memory allocation during model loading. Exploitation requires loading an attacker-controlled or malformed model file. Liquibase Secure bundles pre-packaged, trusted OpenNLP model files at build time; no model files are loaded from external or user-controlled sources at runtime. AbstractModelReader is not imported or called directly in Liquibase code.

statements.status_notes: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail DoS via pathological email address inputs reaching the consumePhrase parser (RFC 5322 phrase parsing). lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation. This vulnerability affects any user using an untrusted module proxy (GOMODPROXY) or checksum database (GOSUMDB). A malicious module proxy can serve altered versions of the Go toolchain. When selecting a different version of the Go toolchain than the currently installed toolchain (due to the GOTOOLCHAIN environment variable, or a go.work or go.mod with a toolchain line), the go command will download and execute a toolchain provided by the module proxy. A malicious module proxy can bypass checksum database validation for this downloaded toolchain.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib toolchain-download checksum validation flaw fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. The Secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the only runtime invocation is `lpm add mysql --global` behind INSTALL_MYSQL (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4 and docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). Repo-wide grep found no runtime `go build`, `go mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN`, `GOMODPROXY`, `GOSUMDB`, `pkg-config`, or `cgo` usage, so the vulnerable toolchain-download path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation.
statements.impact_statement: Go checksum-validation flaw in cmd/go only applies when the Go toolchain downloads modules or toolchains from an untrusted proxy or checksum database. Liquibase Secure installs lpm from a release ZIP (`docker/Dockerfile:39`) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4`). This image does not execute `go`, use GOTOOLCHAIN, or perform module downloads at runtime.

statements.status_notes: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib mime.WordDecoder.DecodeHeader quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35) from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49). The Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). A reachability grep across docker and core found no WordDecoder.DecodeHeader, mime.WordDecoder, encoded-word, MIME header, net/mail, ReadMIMEHeader, or textproto usage, so the vulnerable MIME header decoding path is not reachable from the Liquibase Secure Docker runtime.

statements.status_notes:
Issue summary: A specially crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message could trigger a use-after-free during PKCS#7 signature verification.
Impact summary: A use-after-free may result in process crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution.
When processing a PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message, if the SignedData digestAlgorithms field is present as an empty ASN.1 SET, OpenSSL may incorrectly free a caller-owned BIO during PKCS7_verify(). A subsequent use of the BIO by the calling application results in a use-after-free condition.
In the common case this occurs when the application later calls BIO_free() on the BIO originally passed to PKCS7_verify(). Depending on allocator behavior and application-specific BIO usage patterns, this may result in a crash or other memory corruption. In some application contexts this may potentially be exploitable for remote code execution.
Applications that process PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages using OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs may be affected. Applications using the CMS APIs for this processing are not affected.
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this issue, as the affected code is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, Netty's `DnsResolveContext` insufficiently validates the bailiwick of NS records, enabling DNS Cache Poisoning. An attacker controlling an authoritative name server for a subdomain can poison the cache for parent domains (like `.co.uk`). In `io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.AuthoritativeNameServerList#add` method accepts any NS record from the AUTHORITY section as long as the record's name is a suffix of the questionName. Fixed in pgjdbc 42.7.12. channelBinding is a pgjdbc JDBC URL/connection property; a repo-wide grep (`grep -rn "channelBinding" --include="*.java" --include="*.properties" --include="*.yml" .`) confirms Liquibase's own code never sets it. However, the --url argument is a raw user-supplied JDBC URL passed straight through with no property filtering (DbUrlConnectionCommandStep.java:107-120: `url = commandScope.getArgumentValue(URL_ARG)` flows unmodified into createDatabaseObject()), so a deployment where the user has appended channelBinding=require to their own connection URL — a deliberate, security-conscious choice some users make — remains exposed to this downgrade until the resolved pgjdbc version is 42.7.12+. This is therefore not reachable in Liquibase's *default* configuration, but is reachable if a user opts into channelBinding=require. Independently, the current source already pins the fix by default: pom.xml:62 sets postgresql.version to 42.7.13, and dist/pom.xml:123 consumes that managed version — the scanner reported 42.7.11 on the published 5.2.0 image (built before this version bump).

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains <), DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() validates only the raw container class name (the substring before <) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical() and returns the fully parameterized type without ever validating the nested type arguments against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore place a denied class as a generic type parameter of an allowed container — for example java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget> when only java.util.ArrayList is allow-listed. The container passes the PTV check; com.evil.Gadget is loaded via Class.forName(name, true, loader), instantiated, and its properties are set from attacker-controlled JSON. This completely bypasses an explicitly configured PTV allow-list. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

statements.impact_statement: Netty SPDY zlib header block continues decoding expansion after maxHeaderSize truncation, fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:124, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:307, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:72, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:49, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:50), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable code path is SPDY HEADERS frame zlib decompression in SpdyFrameCodec, part of the legacy SPDY/3.1 protocol decoder that none of Liquibase's Netty consumers negotiate. A focused grep for SpdyFrameCodec, SpdyHeaderBlockDecoder, and io.netty.handler.codec.spdy across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, the SpdyHttpDecoder handler in Netty's SPDY-to-HTTP codec allocates a pooled ByteBuf when processing a client-initiated SYN_STREAM frame with FLAG_FIN=0 and stores the partially constructed FullHttpRequest in messageMap; when the remote peer sends RST_STREAM for that stream or the accumulated content exceeds maxContentLength, the decoder removes the entry but does not release the pooled ByteBuf, causing native memory exhaustion.
statements.impact_statement: Netty SpdyHttpDecoder pooled ByteBuf reference leak on RST_STREAM, fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:124, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:307, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:72, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:49, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:50), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable code path is SpdyHttpDecoder, the SPDY-to-HTTP translation codec, which none of Liquibase's Netty consumers negotiate (they speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 directly). A focused grep for SpdyHttpDecoder, io.netty.handler.codec.spdy, and SpdySessionHandler across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

Netty HTTP/2 decompression ByteBuf reference-count leak in DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener, fixed in 4.1.136.Final / 4.2.16.Final. A remote peer can leak one direct ByteBuf per HTTP/2 DATA frame when a stream's decompressor has already been closed and the error path fails to release the retained buffer — but only in applications that run an HTTP/2 server with content decompression explicitly enabled via DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server and never enables HTTP/2 content decompression. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

statements.status_notes: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 preface timeout issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure is a database migration CLI, not an HTTP server. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5), so the server-side unencrypted HTTP/2 listener required by the advisory is absent.

statements.status_notes: A malicious GOPROXY was previously capable of forging up to two sumdb tiles that allow for a requested module to bypass the GOSUMDB check and persist attacker-controlled module content to a local Go module cache. statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, SQL_REGEX in sqlparse/keywords.py and the per-position loop in sqlparse/lexer.py repeatedly scan unmatched dollar-quoted literal and multiline-comment delimiters, causing quadratic CPU consumption through sqlparse.parse(), sqlparse.format(), and sqlparse.split(). This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: Netty: [Bzip2Decoder] Infinite Loop in RLE State Machine Leads to Event-Loop Thread Hang. The Bzip2Decoder handler in Netty's compression codec pipeline is vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack through a malformed bzip2 stream that permanently captures the event-loop thread in an infinite loop, in the run-length encoding (RLE) state machine within Bzip2BlockDecompressor.read().
statements.impact_statement: Netty Bzip2Decoder infinite loop in the RLE state machine on a malformed bzip2 stream, hanging the event-loop thread. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed 4.1.136.Final release (pom.xml:124, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:49), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. Bzip2Decoder is an opt-in compression codec that must be explicitly added to a Netty pipeline; none of Liquibase's Netty consumers (Cassandra driver via netty-codec, or the Azure/AWS/MongoDB HTTP transports) configure bzip2 compression. A focused grep for Bzip2Decoder, Bzip2Encoder, and io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Bzip2 across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

See CVE-2026-59901 entry on netty-codec above — same root cause (Bzip2Decoder RLE infinite loop), mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-codec-compression (the module Bzip2Decoder lives in for Netty 4.2.x) receive the same not_affected statement. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed 4.2.16.Final release (cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:50, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:72). No Liquibase Netty consumer adds Bzip2Decoder/Bzip2Encoder to a pipeline.

statements.status_notes: Memory leak in Netty's DNS codec when processing malicious DNS response packets containing invalid domain names. The record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before the IDNA-validation exception is thrown, allowing incremental memory exhaustion through sustained malicious DNS responses.
statements.impact_statement: Netty's DNS record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before throwing on domain names that violate IDNA rules, leaking memory per malformed record. Unlike the server-side Netty DNS codec findings above, this path is reached during Liquibase's own outbound DNS resolution, but only triggers when the DNS server answering that resolution (or an on-path attacker able to forge responses) returns malformed records. This requires a compromised or malicious DNS resolution path — an attacker already in a position to forge DNS responses to Liquibase's outbound queries could achieve more direct impact (e.g. redirecting database connections) than a gradual memory leak. No CVE has been assigned to this advisory at the time of assessment. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core's async parser can accumulate excessively long digit sequences (~20,000x amplification of the intended maxNumberLength limit) when input is fed in small chunks without a terminator, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on maxNumberLength.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix for a prior number-length constraint bypass: Jackson's async/non-blocking parser (NonBlockingJsonParser / ByteArrayFeeder) silently buffers digit characters up to maxStringLength instead of enforcing maxNumberLength when input arrives in small chunks without a terminator byte. Found in jackson-core 2.22.0 bundled into liquibase-aws-extension.jar and liquibase-azure.jar. Both extensions are outbound clients that call AWS/Azure APIs and parse the responses those services return over TLS; neither extension's own code invokes Jackson's non-blocking parser API, and neither exposes a network-facing endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled JSON. Exploiting this would require an attacker already able to forge or MITM AWS/Azure API responses, at which point far more direct attacks are already available.

crypto/x509 name-constraint quadratic behavior is not reachable in the Liquibase Secure container. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). A repo-wide search found no code path that parses attacker-controlled certificate chains or invokes the affected x509 name-constraint APIs at runtime.
